item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is materially closer to the frozen contract and has much tighter scope. B adds stronger validation/error tests, but changes retry behavior for every raw reader request and duplicates Files.Add logic, directly conflicting with the required architecture and scope discipline.","reasons":["A reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile and centralizes Add and Upload request construction in one private implementation, preserving option handling and response semantics in one place.","A verifies multipart field name, filename, content, and replay of file-backed uploaded content after a 429.","B modifies RawClient.Do to buffer arbitrary io.Reader bodies across the SDK, despite the explicit instruction not to refactor unrelated request/retry machinery; this also changes memory and reader-consumption behavior globally.","B's Upload reimplements Files.Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing through FilesService.Add as explicitly required, creating duplicate machinery that can drift apart later."],"risks_a":["Upload calls the extracted private add method rather than FilesService.Add literally, so it does not fully satisfy the specified routing contract.","Add now eagerly buffers every body, changing the preserved lower-level API's streaming and source-reader timing behavior.","The visible tests omit required Upload validation and source-reader failure coverage, and validation combines filename and content failures into one less-specific error."],"risks_b":["Global reader buffering changes behavior and memory use for all RawClient requests, not just file uploads.","Upload duplicates Files.Add internals instead of reusing the method required by the contract.","The raw retry changes and related documentation/tests substantially expand scope, including Files.Update behavior expressly outside the requested change."]}
